request.message:
Superbowl
We need to build a workflow...
We will receive two SRT feeds from Grass Valley.
They will each go through Uplynk and land in a single live event for redundancy.
The event is the Super Bowl. We will broadcast it OTT and it will also go out to YouTube as well as to three other syndication partners. YouTube will receive HLS Pull
For the other syndication partners, we will push SRT.

Additionally, another partner is going to feed us an HLS stream and that will follow a different path which will go through Uplynk and into a linear channel with scheduling enabled. This path will go out OTT 24-7.

reply: Set this up with two SRT feeds from Grass Valley both landing in the Super Bowl live event for redundancy, then out to OTT, a YouTube branch via HLS pull, and three partner branches pushing SRT. The HLS partner feed runs a separate path into a scheduled 24/7 channel with its own OTT output, since events and channels can't share one OTT per the platform rules. Worth confirming: I treated the three syndication partners as generic "other platform" destinations — let me know if any of them are actually social or FAST instead.
summary: Built a redundant dual-SRT path from Grass Valley into a single Super Bowl live event feeding OTT, a YouTube syndication branch, and three partner syndication branches, plus a separate HLS partner feed into a scheduled 24/7 linear channel with its own OTT output.

reply: Updated the YouTube branch — it's actually an SRT push to srt://test.bla.bla with 4 audio tracks, not an HLS pull, so I changed that syndication node's protocol and added a note. The Grass Valley note just confirms what's already drawn: both downlinked feeds go into GV, which outputs the dual redundant SRT — no changes needed there. Worth confirming the real destination URL for that YouTube SRT push since "test.bla.bla" was clearly a placeholder.
summary: Switched the YouTube syndication leg from an HLS pull to an SRT push to the given destination with 4 audio tracks, and confirmed the Grass Valley redundancy path.
